source.title: IEPA accredited chemical labs (primary) + IDPH certified water microbiology labs + IEPA private well water testing / LHD path
limitations: Chemical rows transcribed from IEPA Accredited Laboratories Primary Labs PDF (filename document date 12/09/2025). Only in-state primary labs that appear to be commercial/for-hire analytical laboratories are tabulated; wastewater plants, MWRDGC, city water purification, sanitation districts, Rock River Fabrication, AbbVie, American Water Central Lab, and health-dept chemical rows are omitted from the chemical table (health depts appear in the micro health section when listed on the IDPH micro PDF).

IEPA chemical primary PDF does not label Commercial vs non-commercial. Inclusion is a careful name-based filter of clear analytical labs listed in the nightly brief; if unsure whether a primary lab is commercial-for-hire, it was omitted.
Secondary (out-of-state) chemical labs omitted — use the official IEPA PDF/hub.

Microbiological rows transcribed from IDPH Certified Water Microbiology Laboratories PDF (Revision Date Thursday, December 4, 2025). Only in-state Lab Type Commercial and Lab Type Health Department rows are tabulated. Out-of-state Commercial reciprocity rows (starred) omitted.
Private-well acceptance for every commercial chemical and commercial micro row is unknown — call first. Mail vs drop-off unknown.

Verified private-well path is local health departments for coliform bacteria and nitrate per IEPA Well Water Testing page (most LHDs). IEPA does not name individual LHDs that accept samples; call first. Not a single state SPHL path.
ISWS HEAL page states HEAL no longer provides testing services for individual households — not marked as a verified private-well lab.

Precision Water Lab address line on PDF included a glued email; address cleaned to 1705 State Route 161 as printed for the street; email not invented as a contact field beyond what PDF shows for phone.
Phone numbers normalized to (XXX) XXX-XXXX when 10 digits were clear. Addresses kept as printed on the official PDFs (aside from the Precision email glue cleanup).

verified_private_well.name: Illinois local health departments (coliform bacteria and nitrate)
verified_private_well.path: IEPA Well Water Testing page states coliform bacteria and nitrates should be tested yearly and can be done by most local health departments. Find your LHD via the official search/map. Call before collecting — individual LHD acceptance is not named on the IEPA page.
verified_private_well.notes: Not a single state public health laboratory path. ISWS HEAL no longer provides testing for individual households.
